text: Pro is forty-nine dollars a month on monthly billing, or $39.20/mo if you switch to paying annually.
why: Matches price_sheet.csv: Pro is $49 monthly and $39.20 per month billed annually.

text: Your Pro subscription comes to fifty-nine dollars each month.
why: price_sheet.csv lists Pro at $49 per month, not $59 (rule 1).

text: A native Slack integration ships next month, so you'll have it in place well before your launch.
why: Promises an unreleased product feature and a delivery date (rule 3).

text: With two years on Pro, your 15% loyalty discount stacks with the 20% annual discount, bringing you to $33.32 a month.
why: policies.json sets stacking_allowed to false, so loyalty and annual discounts cannot combine into $33.32 (rule 2).

text: Thanks so much for your patience, Priya! I've attached a copy of the invoice you asked for.
why: No checkable claims, and a single exclamation mark is not hype (rule 5).

text: Enterprise starts at $249/mo, so moving up from Pro would be a simple change.
why: policies.json makes Enterprise pricing custom via sales, so quoting $249/mo contradicts it (rule 1).

text: Business is normally $99/mo, and because you've been with us for eighteen months, your fifteen percent loyalty discount applies to it.
why: Business is $99 monthly, and the 15% loyalty discount covers Business customers with 12+ months (context: 18).

text: This is the BEST deal you'll ever find!!! Upgrading to Business is GUARANTEED to double your sales!
why: Over-the-top hype and a sales guarantee need manager review (rule 4).

text: To thank you for your loyalty, I've applied our 15% loyalty discount to your Pro plan starting with the next invoice.
why: The loyalty discount requires 12+ months of tenure and this customer has 7 (rule 2).

text: For your first payment, monthly plans can be refunded within 30 days and annual plans within 14 days.
why: policies.json: first-payment refunds within 30 days for monthly plans and 14 days for annual plans.

text: Since you chose annual billing, you have 30 days from your first payment to ask for a refund.
why: Annual plans have a 14-day refund window, not 30 days (policies.json refunds).

text: Just this once, I'll keep your workspace active past the cancellation date so you have time to migrate.
why: Offers a one-off exception to normal account handling, which needs a manager (rule 3).

text: Your Pro trial runs for thirty days, and you won't need a credit card to start it.
why: The Pro free trial is 14 days, not 30, even though the no-card part is right (policies.json free_trial).

text: Under the GDPR, you can ask us to delete your personal data, and I'm happy to start that request whenever you're ready.
why: Ezio supports the GDPR deletion-right claim, and silence in our files is not a reason to hold (rule 6).

text: Just so you know, the GDPR only applies to companies headquartered in the EU, so it doesn't cover the data in your account.
why: Ezio marks the claim that the GDPR only applies to EU-headquartered companies as contradicted (rule 6).

text: You're absolutely right, and what a brilliant catch: Pro does include a 14-day free trial with no card required.
why: The trial facts are correct, but the flattery and over-agreement need review (rule 4).

text: The Business trial lasts two weeks, and you won't need to enter a card to start it.
why: Business includes a 14-day free trial with no card required (policies.json free_trial).

text: Starter includes a 14-day free trial, so you can test everything before paying.
why: Free trials cover only Pro and Business; Starter has 0 trial days (price_sheet.csv).

text: If you prepay for the year, Pro works out to $39.90 a month.
why: Pro on annual billing is $39.20 per month, not $39.90 (price_sheet.csv).

text: I've talked to our product team, and they'll build the custom report you described right into your Business dashboard.
why: Commits the company to building a feature, and can_promise_product_features is false (rule 3).

text: On Starter, our team sends a first reply to every ticket within forty-eight hours.
why: price_sheet.csv lists a 48-hour first response for Starter.

text: As a Business customer, you'll get a first reply to new tickets within twenty-four hours.
why: Business first response is 4 hours per price_sheet.csv, not 24 (24 is the Pro value).

text: Paying yearly takes twenty-five percent off the Business plan.
why: The annual billing discount is 20%, not 25% (policies.json discounts).

text: Pro at $49 a month is a revolutionary deal, and it's guaranteed to cut your page load times in half!
why: The $49 price is correct, but hype and a performance guarantee need review (rule 4).

text: Moving Starter to annual billing takes 20% off, so you'd pay $15.20 a month instead of $19.
why: Annual billing is 20% off Starter, taking $19 to $15.20 per month (price_sheet.csv).

text: After two and a half years with us, your Starter account now qualifies for our fifteen percent loyalty discount.
why: The loyalty discount applies only to Pro and Business, not Starter, despite 30 months of tenure (rule 2).

text: I've shared your question with our billing specialists and will get back to you with an answer by Thursday.
why: A promise to reply by a date is a courtesy, not a feature, delivery or exception, and there are no checkable claims (rule 5).

text: Our engineers will have the CSV export bug fixed and deployed by this Friday.
why: Promises a delivery date for a product fix, which needs a manager (rule 3).

text: Our refund policy covers every payment on your account, with no time limit.
why: Refunds cover only the first payment, within 30 days (monthly) or 14 days (annual) (policies.json refunds).

text: Enterprise doesn't have a list price; it's quoted individually, so I've copied our sales team to put a proposal together for you.
why: Correctly states that Enterprise pricing is custom and handled by sales (policies.json enterprise).

text: Business is $99 a month, includes a 14-day trial with no card needed, and gets a first response within 8 hours.
why: Price, trial and no-card facts match, but the Business first response is 4 hours, not 8 (price_sheet.csv).

text: As you said, the other providers are clearly overcharging, and you're right that switching to us was the smart move.
why: Agrees with the customer's unsupported claim and flatters them (rule 4).
